name: Shopproof Accessibility: WooCommerce Accessibility Checker and Fixes
author: shopproofapp

sections.description:
Shopproof Accessibility checks the main pages of your WooCommerce shop the way shoppers see them and tells you, in plain words, what is wrong, who it affects and how to fix it.

Since 28 June 2025 the European Accessibility Act (EAA) applies to many online shops that sell to consumers in the EU, through national laws such as the BFSG in Germany and the BaFG in Austria. The technical standard behind them (EN 301 549) builds on WCAG 2.1 level AA. This plugin checks against WCAG 2.0 to 2.2, levels A and AA, and helps you find and fix the technical problems behind those rules. It is free, with no account and no credits.

  • Checks made for shops. Next to general accessibility checks, it looks at the parts of a shop where shoppers who use a keyboard or a screen reader most often get stuck: the product photo, the quantity field, size and colour choices, sale prices, the remove buttons in the cart, and the checkout form.
  • Honest results. A page that could not be checked says “Not checked”, never “fine”. Things no tool can judge, such as whether a photo description makes sense, are listed under “Needs a person” with steps.
  • Fixes in your shop’s code. For problems a plugin can fix safely, there is a fix with its own switch. It changes the page code your shop sends, it never draws over your pages, and it only adds what is missing. All fixes are off until you turn them on, and safe mode turns them all off again.
  • A draft accessibility statement. From your last check it writes a statement in English, German, French, Italian or Dutch: what you work towards, what was checked, the known barriers, how shoppers report a barrier and which authority they can contact in Austria, Germany, France, Italy or the Netherlands. It is saved as a draft page for you to read, change and publish, and it never says your shop is “compliant”.
  • Set up with your AI assistant. Connect Claude Desktop, Cursor or another assistant that supports MCP. It reads your last check, recommends fixes, turns them on after you say yes and writes the statement draft. Off until you turn it on, and every change can be undone.
  • Nothing leaves your site. The check runs in your own browser on your own site. Results are saved in your WordPress database. No account, no credits, no visitor toolbar. The only exception is a message you choose to send us with the Help and contact form.

In your language:

  • Deutsch: Barrierefreiheit für WooCommerce ohne Overlay. Das Plugin prüft Startseite, Produktseite, Warenkorb und Kasse nach WCAG 2.2 (Stufe A und AA), behebt häufige Fehler direkt im Code Ihres Shops und schreibt einen Entwurf Ihrer Barrierefreiheitserklärung. Hilft bei den technischen Anforderungen von BFSG (Deutschland) und BaFG (Österreich). Technische Hilfe, keine Rechtsberatung.
  • Français : accessibilité pour WooCommerce sans overlay : contrôle des pages produit, panier et paiement, corrections dans le code et brouillon de déclaration d’accessibilité.
  • Italiano: accessibilità per WooCommerce senza overlay: controllo di pagine prodotto, carrello e cassa, correzioni nel codice e bozza della dichiarazione di accessibilità.
  • Nederlands: toegankelijkheid voor WooCommerce zonder overlay: controle van productpagina, winkelwagen en afrekenen, oplossingen in de code en een concept toegankelijkheidsverklaring.

What it does not do:

  • It does not make your shop “compliant” with any law. Automatic checks find some problems, not all of them.
  • It does not add an overlay or a toolbar for visitors.
  • It does not change your shop unless you turn on a fix.

This is technical help, not legal advice.

External services

This plugin uses one outside service, and only when you press “Send message” in the Help and contact form at the end of its Accessibility screen. The accessibility check itself sends nothing anywhere.

  • What it is: the Shopproof contact service at https://shopproof.app/api/contact, run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH (Austria) on Amazon Web Services in Frankfurt. It passes your message on as an email to support@shopproof.app so we can answer you, and keeps no other copy.
  • What is sent, and when: only when you press “Send message”, your site sends your name (if you give it), your email address, your message, your shop address (if you leave that tick on), the plugin and axe-core versions, and the WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP and theme versions.
  • Terms of use: https://shopproof.app/terms/
  • Privacy notice: https://shopproof.app/privacy/#contact

Third-party libraries

The check uses axe-core 4.14.0 by Deque Systems, Inc., licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, shipped unchanged in assets/vendor/axe-core/ with its licence files. Source: https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core/tree/v4.14.0 and https://www.npmjs.com/package/axe-core/v/4.14.0
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Go to WooCommerce, Accessibility.
  3. Press “Check my shop”.

To include the cart and checkout, put a product in your cart in the same browser first.
sections.faq:
Is the accessibility statement legally enough?

It is a starting point written from your own check, not legal advice. Read it, change what is not right for your shop, and ask an adviser if you are unsure whether the European Accessibility Act applies to you. The plugin only saves it as a draft and never overwrites a statement page you published or changed.

Does it send my pages anywhere?

No. The check runs in your browser, and the results are stored in your own WordPress database. The plugin makes no requests to any outside server, except when you send us a message with the Help and contact form (see below). To check a page, the plugin opens it in a hidden frame in your browser, the same as a visit. Anything your pages load themselves, such as an analytics or chat script, loads as it does on any visit, so a check can show up in your visitor statistics.

How do I get help or contact you?

At the end of the Accessibility screen, under “Help and contact”, there are our guides, the support forum here on WordPress.org and a short form. Only when you press “Send message” does your site send your name, email address and message, your shop address (if you leave that tick on) and the plugin, WordPress, WooCommerce, PHP and theme versions to shopproof.app, our own service run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH. It reaches us as an email to support@shopproof.app and keeps no other copy. We use it only to answer you. Privacy notice: https://shopproof.app/privacy/#contact. You can also write to support@shopproof.app from your own email.

What if a finding is wrong?

Under each finding there is an “Is this wrong? Tell us” link. It opens your own email app with a message to support@shopproof.app that names the check, where it was found, and the plugin, axe-core and theme versions. You can change it before sending, and nothing is sent unless you press Send. We use these reports to remove false alarms.

Can I see what a fix does before I turn it on?

Yes. Press “Preview” next to the fix. The plugin checks your shop again in your own browser with only that fix added, and tells you how many places the check finds with it. Shoppers see no change and nothing is saved.

A fix changed something I did not want. How do I undo it?

Turn that fix off and press “Save fixes”, or turn on safe mode to turn all fixes off at once. If you cannot reach the screen, add define( 'SHOPPROOF_A11Y_SAFE_MODE', true ); to wp-config.php.

Why does a page say “Not checked”?

The page could not be opened, took too long, sent the check elsewhere (for example the checkout with an empty cart), or does not exist. Fix the cause and check again.

Does this help AI shopping agents?

Some of it can. AI agents that read the page code rely on the same button names, link names and labels as screen readers, so fixes like names for icon links and for search and close buttons help them too. We make no promise about AI visibility or sales.

Can my AI assistant set this up for me?

Yes, if it can use MCP servers from a config file (for example Claude Desktop or Cursor). Turn it on under WooCommerce > Accessibility > AI assistant and create a connection key. The assistant can read your last check, turn on the fixes it calls for and write your statement draft. It shows you each change first, and every change can be undone. It cannot run the check, publish a page or delete anything. Your assistant connects to your shop; the plugin sends nothing. A connection key works only for this connection, not for the rest of your site, and stops working after 90 days, when a daily cleanup deletes it. Switching the connection off or deactivating the plugin deletes every key. Your site needs HTTPS for keys. On a multisite network, keys can be made only when the plugin is network active.

Is my shop accessible when no problems are found?

Not necessarily. Automatic checks catch only part of the problems. Work through the “Needs a person” list as well.
sections.changelog:
0.5.0

  • New: AI assistant connection (MCP), off until you turn it on. Your own AI assistant can read the last check, recommend and turn on fixes, and write the statement draft, always after showing you the change. Every change is listed on the screen and can be undone. Connection keys work only for this connection, for 90 days, and are deleted when you switch it off or deactivate the plugin. The plugin sends nothing anywhere; the assistant connects to your shop.

0.4.0

  • Behind the scenes: small hooks so the separate Pro add-on can reuse this plugin’s check and keep a copy of each saved statement. One line in the Help and contact box names the Pro add-on and links to its page (hidden once Pro is active). Nothing new is sent anywhere.

0.3.0

  • A clearer Accessibility screen with five tabs: Overview, Problems, Needs a person, Fixes and Statement. The page is much shorter and opens on a summary with what to do next.
  • Problems are short rows you open one at a time. The ones this plugin can fix come first, and you can turn on the fix and preview it right inside the problem.
  • Fixes are cards with an On/Off switch that is saved at once. Fixes that match your last check say “Recommended for your shop”.
  • The accessibility statement helper now goes in 3 steps: your details, read the text, save as a draft page.
  • New “Help and contact” box at the end of the screen: guides, the support forum and a short form to send us a message. Nothing is sent until you press “Send message”. “Is this wrong?” reports now go to support@shopproof.app.

0.2.0

  • New fix “Name search and close buttons”: a search icon button or a popup close button with no name gets “Search”, “Close search” or “Close”, only when its own code says what it does. Off until you turn it on.
  • New checks: search and close buttons with no name, and size or colour swatches that cannot be used with a keyboard.

0.1.0

First version.

  • Check of the home, shop, product, cart, checkout and account pages with axe-core and checks made for WooCommerce, in plain English, with a “Needs a person” list for what no tool can judge.
  • Check any other page of your shop on demand (shown on the screen, not saved).
  • Shop checks: the cart drawer takes the keyboard focus, “added to cart” and other shop messages are read out, checkout field errors reach screen readers, product list buttons and icon links have names, required checkout fields are marked.
  • No false alarms from loading placeholders or fade ins: the check waits for the cart and checkout blocks to load and for cookie banners to finish fading in before it measures.
  • Places where the accessibility rules make an exception the general check cannot see (a count badge on a cart button, a phone number on its own line, a breadcrumb, text in a logo, the browser’s own checkbox, a small link next to a bigger one to the same page) are listed under “Needs a person” instead of as problems.
  • Ten fixes, each with its own switch and all off at first: shop messages read out, product name on remove buttons, keyboard access to the store notice, autofill on checkout fields, product photo descriptions, old and new price told apart, a name for the quantity field, product list buttons named with the words they show, names for icon links (logo, phone, email, social sites), names for size and colour choices. Safe mode turns them all off.
  • “Preview” for each fix: checks your shop again with only that fix and shows how many places are left, without saving anything or changing what shoppers see.
  • Accessibility statement helper: a draft statement page in English, German, French, Italian or Dutch, written from your last check.
  • “Is this wrong? Tell us” link under each finding, which prepares an email in your own email app.
